entries.title: Odd greedy expansions can terminate after arbitrarily many steps
entries.report_scope: For every odd prime p, the odd greedy algorithm applied to 2/(2(p-1)!-1) terminates with reduced positive numerators 2,3,...,p-1,1 and therefore exactly p-1 unit fractions, by Pihko Theorem3.5. This gives an explicit unbounded-length terminating family, not universal termination.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed verify.py for source-family primes3,5,7,11,13 using exact Fraction arithmetic. Reduced numerators and term counts2,4,6,10,12 match; exact reconstruction and the preceding-odd-denominator test verify every greedy choice. The largest tested denominator has58103 bits. The infinite family remains the credited source theorem. Standard-library exact Python, Apache-2.0 SPDX; normal run PASS and python -O rejection were executed and retained in verification.json/verification_output.txt.

entries.title: Exact Tunnell obstructions with the conditional direction kept separate
entries.report_scope: For positive squarefree n, unequal signed ternary-form counts in Tunnell’s criterion prove n is not congruent, unconditionally. Equality is only reported as a BSD-conditional converse. The attached exact counting certificate classifies these necessary conditions through5000; it does not unconditionally classify all congruent numbers.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed verify.py for all3042 positive squarefree n<=5000, with all four signed-form counts independently checked by full signed enumeration for every0<=n<=120. Exactly1275 fail Tunnell’s necessary test;1767 merely pass it. Exact per-n evidence is tunnell_counts.json; passing is not an unconditional congruence certificate. Standard-library exact Python, Apache-2.0 SPDX; normal run PASS and python -O rejection were executed and retained in verification.json/verification_output.txt.
execution_generated_files: A future user execution writes tunnell_counts.json beside verify.py. This generated output is not part of the prepared payload.
checked_references: J.B.Tunnell, Invent.Math.72(1983),323–334, original primary PDF and indexed text, https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~zeilberg/EM22/JT1983.pdf

entries.title: Every composite super-Wieferich candidate needs a prime factor exceeding100000
entries.report_scope: For odd n>1 with p^e exactly dividing n, n^2 divides2^(n-1)-1 iff every p satisfies ord_p(2)|(n-1) and v_p(2^(p-1)-1)>=2e. Exact enumeration of all primes<=100000 then proves that any composite candidate must have a prime factor>100000. Existence of composite candidates is not settled.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed verify.py: sieve independently matches trial primality for all integers<=100000 (9592 primes); only1093,3511 pass the Wieferich test, each valuation is2, their exact orders are364,1755, and their sole composite product fails. The local iff also agrees with direct modular exponentiation for every odd3<=n<=2001. Infinite prime-support exclusion rests on the proof. Standard-library exact Python, Apache-2.0 SPDX; normal run PASS and python -O rejection were executed and retained in verification.json/verification_output.txt.
checked_references: Self-contained lifting/order argument and exhaustive exact prime-support certificate in this folder

entries.title: Recognition and Characterization of Leaf Powers
entries.report_scope: For every fixed k≥5, graphs whose quotient by equal closed neighborhoods is a forest have explicit k-leaf roots, constructible in polynomial time; the test is sufficient, not a recognition test for all leaf powers.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Complexity of Dense Perfect Hypergraph Matching
entries.report_scope: For fixed c>1/3, sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraphs with n divisible by three and minimum codegree≥cn have a polynomial-time perfect-matching decision algorithm consisting of one explicit GF(2) linear-system test.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.
checked_references: Peter Keevash, Fiachra Knox, Richard Mycroft, Polynomial-Time Perfect Matchings in Dense Hypergraphs, STOC2013 primary author paper, Theorem 1.4 and discussion of its special 3-uniform scope, pp.1–2: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/keevash/papers/stoc212fp-keevash.pdf . Full revised paper arXiv:1307.2608v2, Adv.Math.269 (2015), pp.265–334; this report fixes the STOC theorem numbering.

entries.title: Optimal Algebraic Immunity of Boolean Functions
entries.report_scope: For every n≥16 and 1≤m≤n, some Boolean map f:F₂ⁿ→F₂ᵐ has graph algebraic immunity at least floor(n/16)+1; this is nonconstructive and does not prove the optimum dimension bound.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Quadratic graph diameter for every simple graphical zonotope
entries.report_scope: Every graphical zonotope of a connected simple graph on d+1 vertices, and every invertible affine image, has vertex-edge diameter at most |E| <= d(d+1)/2.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed check_exact.py with assertions enabled: PASS 771 connected labelled simple graphs on2..5vertices; exact all-pairs orientation-graph diameters. python -O was separately executed and refused. These are finite exact checks only.

entries.title: ICP for rooted arborescences on bidirected cactus graphs
entries.report_scope: For every connected undirected cactus, replace every edge by both directed arcs. Its outward arborescence polytope at any root has ICP for every integer dilation.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed check_exact.py with assertions enabled: PASS 400 weighted bidirected-cactus dilate decompositions; physical rooted-tree reconstruction and exact affine-rank oracle. python -O was separately executed and refused. These are finite exact checks only.

entries.title: Greedy Decomposition of the Spanning-Tree Polytope
entries.report_scope: Under the usual greedy range 0≤λ≤k, every scaled integral point of the spanning-tree polytope of K_{2,t}, t≥2, admits positive integral greedy subtraction; a polynomial-time decomposition uses at most 5t+1 steps.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Polynomial-Time Minimization of K-Submodular Functions
entries.report_scope: Explicit k-submodular functions given by admissible unary terms and nonnegative star-metric pair interactions on a tree can be minimized exactly in O(n(k+1)²) rational operations, with polynomial bit complexity.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Hardness of Path-Cost Arborescence Optimization
entries.report_scope: Distinguishing optimum zero is NP-hard for destination-specific path-cost spanning arborescences even on DAGs with indegree≤2, outdegree≤2, underlying undirected degree≤3 and only 0/1 costs.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Subquadratic Approximation for Longest Common Subsequences
entries.report_scope: For matching-position count r, an exact longest common subsequence is computable in O((n+r) log(n+2)) word operations after alphabet compression; r=n^{2−Ω(1)} gives a truly subquadratic exact regime.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.
checked_references: J. W. Hunt and T. G. Szymanski, A Fast Algorithm for Computing Longest Common Subsequences, Communications of the ACM 20(5), 1977, pp.350–353, DOI https://doi.org/10.1145/359581.359603 . Primary paper bibliographic/algorithm statement checked; the chain and tails correctness are proved here.

entries.title: Complexity of Approximate Counting in Spin Systems
entries.report_scope: For fixed q≥2 and a supplied feedback vertex set S of size k, exact rational Potts and hard-core partition functions are computable in q^k·poly(L) and 2^k·poly(L) bit time, respectively, where G−S is a forest and L is full encoded input length.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Algorithms for Symmetry-Reduced Semidefinite Programs
entries.report_scope: A rational SDP whose coefficient matrices are invariant under all simultaneous row/column permutations reduces exactly to a two-variable rational LP, allowing exact feasibility/optimality/unboundedness decisions in polynomial bit time.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Approximating Submodular Functions by Matroid Rank Functions
entries.report_scope: Every integer-valued normalized monotone submodular function with f({i})=1 is exactly a matroid rank function, so the prompt’s comparison holds with α=1 in this integral regime.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Compact Representations of Four-Thirds Near-Mincuts
entries.report_scope: Every cut of a connected nonnegatively weighted cactus with 0<λ and weight≤4λ/3 is one bridge or one pair of edges in one cycle; all such cuts have an O(n+m)-word implicit representation.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Deterministic Optimization of Top-$k$ Perfect-Matching Edges
entries.report_scope: On arbitrary graphs with two rational weight levels a<b, one polynomial-time perfect matching maximizes the sum of its k largest edge weights simultaneously for every k, including k supplied as input.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.
checked_references: Edmonds 1965, primary NIST paper, abstract and weighted algorithm: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/jres/69B/jresv69Bn1-2p125_A1b.pdf .

entries.title: Finite-field polynomial multiplication and integer-multiplication lower bounds
entries.report_scope: For every fixed C≥1 and primes d≤p≤d^C, d≥2, degree<d polynomial multiplication over F_p takes O(d log p·log(d log p)) bit time using credited O(N log N) integer multiplication and explicit carry-free packing.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.
checked_references: Harvey–van der Hoeven, Annals of Mathematics 193 (2021), primary publication abstract/theorem: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2021/193-2/p04 ; author paper page https://web.maths.unsw.edu.au/~davidharvey/research/nlogn/index.html .

entries.title: Exact containment when the outer zonotope has fixed generator co-rank
entries.report_scope: For rational full-row-rank H in Q^(d x m), centered zonotope containment is decidable in binom(m,d-1) poly(L) bit operations. With m=d+c and fixed c this is polynomial in total encoded input length L.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed check_exact.py with assertions enabled: PASS 120 rational containment cases d1..4, outer co-rank0..2; independent cube-feasibility oracle. python -O was separately executed and refused. These are finite exact checks only.

entries.title: Approximating Fare-Zone Assignment on Trees
entries.report_scope: Exact hard-budget fare-zone optimization is NP-hard even on stars with edge congestion exactly three, all commodity weights and budgets one, and paths of length one or two.

entries.title: An explicit anticanonical count on every open subset of projective space
entries.report_scope: For every n>=1 and every fixed nonempty Zariski open U in P^n/Q, with H([x])=max|x_i|^(n+1) on primitive integer coordinates, N(U,B)~2^n B/zeta(n+1), with error O_U(B^(n/(n+1))) for n>=2 and O_U(B^(1/2) log B) for n=1.

entries.report_scope: For every fixed depth D≥2, unbounded-fan-in AND/OR/NOT circuits outputting exact n-bit integer products need exp(Ω_D((n/log(n+2))^{1/(D−1)})) gates; no unrestricted-depth lower bound is claimed.

entries.title: Perfect-Matching Search in Deterministic NC (General Graphs)
entries.report_scope: Perfect-matching search, including the NO output, is in logspace-uniform NC² on forests, by computing edge-cut parities in parallel and verifying the resulting candidate matching.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: A complete exact universal-tensor-square search through degree sixteen
entries.report_scope: For every 1≤n≤16 outside {2,4,9}, an explicit irreducible S_n representation has a tensor square containing every irreducible; no such representation exists at the three excluded degrees in this finite range.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Complete exact symmetric-group character tables and universal-square candidate searches passed for n=1..16; every character entry for n=1..7 also matched a separate Frobenius coefficient oracle. Hook-length degrees, full row orthogonality, integral nonnegative multiplicities and dimension sums passed. -O was run and rejected; full witness spectra and execution logs retained.

Published Advances in Mathematics 288 (2016), 702–731. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1304.0738v2

[2] Alexander R. Miller, On parity and characters of symmetric groups, Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 162 (2019), 231–240, DOI 10.1016/j.jcta.2018.11.001. Author manuscript Section 1.1, equations (1) and (2), explicitly states both the Vandermonde/power-sum Frobenius coefficient formula and the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule used by the two independent implementations. These formulas on manuscript p.1 were freshly inspected; no full-paper proof review is claimed. https://www.armiller.org/Parity.pdf

entries.title: Isometric L1 embeddings of all positively weighted cactus metrics
entries.report_scope: Every finite connected cactus with arbitrary positive edge lengths embeds isometrically in real L1; it has a tree decomposition with bag cardinality at most3, giving distortion1 on this explicit bag-size3 subclass.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: Executed check_exact.py with assertions enabled: PASS 140 rational weighted cacti; 15202 pairwise L1 distances equal independent Dijkstra shortest paths. python -O was separately executed and refused. These are finite exact checks only.

entries.title: Polynomial switch-chain mixing for all degree sequences
entries.report_scope: For the all-one degree sequence on even n≥4, the literal lazy four-vertex switch chain has gap at least 1/(12 binom(n,4)) and mixes by ceil(12 binom(n,4) ln(4n/2)), hence by 2n⁸.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Almost-linear edit-distance approximation scheme
entries.report_scope: Exact unit-cost edit distance on the promise ED(x,y)≤k is computable in O(N(k+1)) word operations and O(k+1) working words; k=N^{o(1)} gives deterministic almost-linear exact estimation.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Depth-five homogeneous lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication
entries.report_scope: A monotone homogeneous depth-three ΣΠΣ circuit for IMM_{n,n}, whose product gates multiply n homogeneous linear forms with nonnegative real coefficients, requires at least n^{n−1} product gates for n≥2.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Integer multiplication below n log n
entries.report_scope: A uniform deterministic fixed-multitape algorithm multiplies n-bit operands in O(n(h+1)) bit time and O(n) work bits when one operand has Hamming weight h; h≤√log₂(n+2) meets the prompt’s time scale.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Almost-linear maximum-cardinality matching
entries.report_scope: Maximum-cardinality matching is deterministic exact in O(D·2^p·poly(p,log(n+D+2))) word operations from a supplied nice path decomposition of length D and bag size at most p; D=N^{1+o(1)}, p=o(log N) give almost-linear time.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.

entries.title: Randomized k-server with squared-logarithmic ratio
entries.report_scope: On a unit uniform metric with k initially distinct server sites, randomized marking has E[cost]≤2H_k·OPT with additive constant zero for every fixed finite request sequence.
entries.recorded_verification_summary: An exact standard-library checker accompanies this report; its actual tested ranges and stdout are recorded in verification.json and verification_stdout.txt.
